description:
#314 family F-E.  ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED s396 — the refusal is RIGHT until the
missing piece below exists.  Everything here is measured; do not re-derive it.

THE REFUSAL (Pl/Parser2.pm, _lower_our_decl):

    die "Parser2 TODO: our '$n' shadows a my-lexical\n"
      if $self->{_let_bound_vars}{$n};

Its comment says a `defvar` of a let-bound name would proclaim it special and
poison the lexical lets — true, and OBSOLETE for the ordinary partition since
direction D (#289): an ordinary package global is a `p-defcell` symbol macro,
and a `let` of a symbol-macro name is legal CL that shadows it.  So narrowing
the refusal to `Pl::GlobalPartition::is_exception_global($n)` makes the file
compile.  comp/our.t then goes TRANSPILE-FAIL (0 of 7) -> 7/7 OK.

BUT THAT IS A SILENT WRONG, and the probe says so.  `our $y` INTRODUCES the
package variable for the rest of its scope; a use after it must stop reading
the `my $y` it shadows.  Eight shapes vs perl 5.40.3, PCL after the narrowing:

    $y=1; { my $y=2; { our $y = $y; print $y } }   perl 2   PCL 2   (coincidence)
    ... then print $::y                            perl 2   PCL 1   WRONG
    $z=10; { my $z=20; { our $z; print $z } }      perl 10  PCL 20  WRONG
    @w=(1,2); { my @w=(3,4); { our @w; print "@w" } }  perl "1 2"  PCL "3 4"
    %h=(a=>1); { my %h=(b=>2); { our %h; print keys %h } }  perl a  PCL b
    sub f { my $q=5; { our $q = 9; } return $q }   perl pkg=9  PCL pkg=0

comp/our.t's own 7 rows all pass anyway (row 7's answer coincides), so THE
FILE PASSING IS NOT EVIDENCE the change is right — this is the case where a
green file hides the divergence.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX DOES NOT WORK (tried, measured, reverted).  Qualifying the
declaration and the uses it covers — `$y` -> `$::y`, via _rename_decl_within,
which already skips the decl's own RHS and stops at a later declaration — emits
`main::$z` where the shadowed use was.  It still reads 20, because
**`main::$z` and `$z` are THE SAME CL SYMBOL**: the qualifier is the CL reader's
package prefix, and the section is already `in-package MAIN`.  A `let` of that
symbol shadows every spelling of it.  Qualification cannot escape a lexical
binding; only a different FORM can.

SO THE MISSING PIECE IS ONE OF:
  (a) an explicit global-read/write FORM — `(sb-ext:symbol-global-value '$z)`,
      i.e. what the p-defcell symbol macro expands to — emitted for a use the
      `our` covers, so it reaches the cell past the live `let`.  Needs an
      emitter path and a `local`-compatible setf; check what p-local-cell does.
  (b) rename the MY instead of the our (`$z__shadow__N`), which is the existing
      my-shadow machinery — but the `our` is typically in a NESTED block and
      the `my` is outer, so the rename region is the outer one, i.e. a bigger
      and riskier edit than it looks.

POPULATION: comp/our.t (7 rows) is the only companion-suite file.  That is a
poor return on either fix ON ITS OWN — but (a) is plausibly the same primitive
#291/#296 need, so fold it in there rather than building it for 7 rows.

BAR when built: the eight probe shapes above must match perl, not just
comp/our.t's plan; then corpus-diff, gate, full sweep.
subject: our-shadows-my (#314 F-E): narrowing the refusal is a SILENT WRONG - needs a global-read FORM, not a qualified NAME
